title: Product opportunity portfolio manager

stages.name: reconstructNeeds
stages.algorithm: Reconcile customer requests into underlying outcomes and constraints. Separate a suggested implementation from the need it serves; preserve segments whose superficially similar requests arise from different workflows and require different interventions.
stages.gate: Every need has attributable evidence; invented segments and unsupported market sizes are forbidden.

stages.name: generateInterventions
stages.algorithm: Propose materially different ways to improve each outcome, including process, service, and product changes. Explain the mechanism, affected users, and expected tradeoffs; avoid generating cosmetic variants that all depend on the same untested assumption.
stages.gate: Candidate set includes a credible low-change baseline and distinct mechanisms.

stages.name: estimateDependencies
stages.algorithm: Translate each intervention into bounded work packages, request estimates from authorized sources, and identify shared enabling work. Preserve cost ranges and unknowns rather than inventing precision; inspect whether dependencies make apparently independent projects coupled.
stages.gate: Shared work is costed once; missing estimates remain explicit and block firm commitments.

stages.name: constructPortfolios
stages.algorithm: Submit eligible options and exact constraints to a portfolio solver, then interpret feasible alternatives against the supplied strategy. Explain who benefits and what is deferred; generate contingency portfolios for major assumption changes rather than a single opaque ranking.
stages.gate: Exact budget and capacity feasibility; ranking rationale uses supplied priorities only.

stages.name: planLearning
stages.algorithm: Choose the cheapest credible experiment capable of changing a portfolio decision. State how positive, negative, and inconclusive results would alter the selected work, and schedule learning before irreversible dependent commitments wherever feasible.
stages.gate: An experiment has an actionable decision rule and does not merely collect agreeable feedback.

operational_details: A sponsor changes priorities mid-cycle: fork the scenario and preserve the approved baseline.
Two projects claim the same benefit: identify overlap instead of summing both estimates.
A dependency estimate is missing: show a contingent portfolio, not false feasibility.
A customer quote supports several needs: preserve one source and avoid multiplying evidence strength.
An experiment is inconclusive: retain the uncertainty rather than treating it as a failed idea.
representative_episode: Three opportunities share an identity-system dependency, and a cheaper service change may solve the same need as a major feature.
independent_truth_basis: Hidden benefit overlap and costs with exact feasible portfolios; human comparison of intervention diversity and usefulness.
